opened_skills.name: go-api-contracts
opened_skills.reason: The supported CLI input grammar, file output, exit status, diagnostics and prefix-retention contract change from one record to ordered batches. Preserve single-record behavior and Go 1.22.

opened_skills.name: go-behavior-tests
opened_skills.reason: This is meaningful batch behavior with requested success and failure tests; assertions must observe the accepted prefix and absence of later effects at both helper and real executable boundaries.

opened_skills.name: go-core-style
opened_skills.reason: Writing and testing Go production code requires idiomatic control flow, contextual errors, standard-library dependencies and formatting.

opened_skills.name: go-interfaces-and-composition
opened_skills.reason: Protecting accepted duplicate values from partial writes introduces temporary-file ownership and close, rename and cleanup lifetimes. A concrete helper owns those resources; no new interface is needed.

opened_references.reason: Choose actual during-write failure and retained-state checks rather than treating an open obstruction as proof of partial-write safety.

not_opened.name: go-package-boundaries
not_opened.reason: No packages, import directions or responsibility ownership change. A private record-write helper remains within the existing CLI package.

scope: Only the authorized dispatch, assigned module and relevant offered guidance were read; no other author workspace or repository content was inspected.
